body:
I think it makes sense to talk about enqueuing a reaction as entering a triple of (element, definition, which ∈ { upgrade, connected, … }, extra stuff) with the observation that for a given element you'll only ever see one definition. Because the queues are per-element, the element is implied, but as @cbrewster points out the element's definition isn't set.

The way WebKit has it (for example, [here](https://github.com/WebKit/webkit/blob/7bd19bbe68f3a8bef79454d215b7679cfd2b5c6f/Source/WebCore/dom/Element.cpp#L1960)); the element is associated with its queue, and the queue with a definition. Blink and Gecko do it equivalently but structurally differently where reactions hold onto a definition ([Blink,](https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/third_party/WebKit/Source/core/html/custom/CustomElementReaction.h?sq=package:chromium) [Gecko](https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/file/c15e2f280729/dom/base/CustomElementRegistry.cpp#l1056))

The most important thing here is not messing up the timing of when selectors apply differently and what happens on failure.
